statement: For every input y and (i,s) in [m] x {0,1}^r: i wins at s iff all K_{k,m} tests pass, namely (a) X_i[b]=1 for each b; (b) for each j != i, X_j[p_{i,s,j}]=0; (c) for each h and each non-input gate, the claimed value equals the gate function of its predecessors, read from the transcript or from A_{i,h}; (d) for each h, claimed d=1 and claimed b=s_h. Each test is computed by a deterministic adaptive bit-query decision tree of depth at most max(3,l+1), which is l+1 for m>=4: a pointer test reads l pointer bits, then the one target bit they select, while gate tests read at most three fixed bits. A pointer test is not a function of a small fixed set of bits: it can depend on all l+m pointer and target coordinates.
